the evidence does not support or refute the hypothesis that the administration of a single intravenous dose of 1.0 g of calcium gluconate to a patient with a serum calcium of less than 7.0 mg/dl is associated with a reduction in the incidence of cardiac arrest or death.

the use of the 2nd and 3rd generations of cephalosporins should be restricted to patients with a history of penicillin allergy, or to those in whom the use of penicillin has failed, because of the high frequency of penicillin-resistant organisms in the community.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the hepatic resection for metastatic ovarian cancer is a feasible and safe treatment option for patients with recurrent metastatic ovarian cancers.
the hepatic resection for metastatic ovarian cancer is a safe and effective procedure for selected patients.
the hepatic resection is a safe and effective therapy for recurrent metastatic epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a 2D or a 3D ultrasound probe for the diagnosis of ovarian cancer does not significantly influence the diagnostic performance of the test.

we have shown that a combination of a drug that targets the tumor vasculature (bevacizumab) with a drug that targets a specific molecular pathway in the tumor cells (everolimus), has a very strong effect in a mouse model of metastatic ovarian cancer.
there is no evidence of benefit from resection of hepatic metastases from ovarian cancer, and there is a risk of increased mortality.
